label: About
headline: Engineer first, measured second
intro: I build production web apps across the whole stack — TypeScript on React/Next.js and Angular on the frontend, Node.js and NestJS on the backend, deployed on GCP, Cloudflare and Vercel. Three years of it inside product teams.
What I care about is the part after merge: whether the change moved a number, what it cost to run, and what it will cost the next person to maintain.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: English C1 reading/listening, B2 speaking (EF SET) · Ukrainian, Russian native

principles.label: How I work

items.title: End-to-end ownership
items.body: Comfortable taking a feature from architecture decision through database schema, API, frontend, CI/CD and post-release monitoring. Shipping means it's live and observed, not merged.

items.title: Decisions backed by data
items.body: Product analytics and feature flags as part of the normal workflow. Ran 10+ A/B experiments on conversion funnels rather than shipping on intuition.

items.title: AI-assisted workflow
items.body: Custom prompts and context setups built into daily development to cut boilerplate and accelerate delivery — a deliberate process, not an occasional tool.

principles.note: Day to day that runs inside structured team workflows — planning, code review, iterative delivery, and regular collaboration with designers.

entries.title: Starting computer science in Zaporizhzhia
entries.body: Enrolled at the Polytechnic National University with no real code behind me. The first year was algorithms on paper and C++ in a lab, and the first thing that stuck was how much faster I learned when I had something to ship.

entries.title: A puzzle game built in Unity
entries.body: Spent a few months on a puzzle game in Unity and C# — several levels, working mechanics, an APK you could install and actually play. First time I took something past the interesting part and finished it.

entries.title: Internship at GroupBWT
entries.body: First time working inside a real process: Jira tickets, code review, a mentor reading everything I wrote. Shipped features across frontend, backend and admin panel, and learned to size work honestly.

entries.title: Binary Studio Academy
entries.body: Three months of full stack work at a pace that left no room for gaps: React, Express, Docker, WebSockets, tests expected rather than optional. Most of what I know about learning a stack quickly comes from that summer.

entries.title: Vibe Barbershop
entries.body: A friend's barbershop needed a site, and it became the first thing I built that someone paid for and real customers used. Two locations, an admin panel the owners still update themselves. Short project, but the first one where shipping it wrong had consequences beyond a grade.

entries.title: ArtWizard
entries.body: First salaried job. Joined as the only developer on a platform for discovering cultural events and built it from an empty repository — Next.js on the front, NestJS behind it. Worked directly with a designer on a shared UI kit, which was the first time someone else's decisions had to render exactly right.

entries.title: Joining a product team at Coverr
entries.body: Moved from building features to owning them: an Angular and NestJS microservice platform with paying users, analytics on every funnel, and infrastructure decisions with a monthly bill attached.

entries.title: Moving to Varna
entries.body: Relocated to the Bulgarian coast and settled into remote work across European time zones.

now.label: Now
now.heading: Based in Varna, Bulgaria
now.body: Working remotely on EET, which overlaps comfortably with most European teams and part of the US morning. Open to a new full-time role — remote, or on-site here in Varna — ideally on a product with real users and real numbers to move.
